name: Bad Mergentheim (Baden-Württemberg, Germany)
administrative_context: Bad Mergentheim (then Mergentheim) was the headquarters of the Teutonic Order's Deutschmeister—the Grand Master of the German branch of the Teutonic Order. As a religious-military order's administrative center, it had its own jurisdictional apparatus distinct from standard ecclesiastical or secular territories. The 1628-1629 trials at Mergentheim occurred within this Order's territorial jurisdiction.
witchcraft_trials_significance: The Mergentheim witch trials of 1628-1629 were part of the broader wave of south German prosecution that peaked in those years alongside the Bamberg, Würzburg, and Ellwangen panics. The trials occurred within the Teutonic Order's territorial jurisdiction, making them an unusual instance of military-religious order prosecution. The case demonstrates the geographic spread of the 1626-1631 south German persecution wave beyond the major episcopal territories.

scholarly_analysis.clark_perspective: The Mergentheim case illustrates the geographic diffusion of the 1626-1631 German persecution wave beyond the major episcopal centers into smaller territories with diverse institutional structures.
scholarly_analysis.hutton_perspective: Hutton situates Mergentheim within the pattern of regional witch panic spread, noting how prosecution in one major territory created pressure in adjacent areas through judicial communication, fleeing suspects crossing borders, and general fear.
scholarly_analysis.ginzburg_perspective: As a peripheral case in the broader south German persecution wave, Mergentheim illustrates the geographic extent to which the interrogation-shaped confession template was transmitted across territorial boundaries.

legacy_and_historiographical_importance: Mergentheim appears in the broader surveys of south German witch persecution as part of the 1626-1631 wave. It is less extensively studied as an individual case than the major episcopal centers.
primary_sources: Teutonic Order administrative records; analyzed in broader south German witch hunt surveys
source_method: Published scholarship (Behringer, Levack), Teutonic Order archival sources
scholarly_disagreement: The precise scale and character of the Mergentheim prosecution is less well documented in the accessible scholarship than the major episcopal cases; confidence in specific details is accordingly lower.
